body:
TRUST-ROOT. `plugins/adlc-claude-code/hooks/handoff-resolve.mjs` (shipped by T157 / PR #476) resolves `@adlc/context-handoff` by walking into the **project's** `node_modules` and then dynamic-imports the result inside an enforcing PreToolUse hook. Slice 5 (PR #477) copies that resolver into the Codex plugin, so two enforcing hooks now execute project-controlled code.

Raised as CRITICAL by `adversarial-review --provider codex` on PR #477 across two rounds. It is NOT introduced by that PR — it is the slice-4 resolver design — so it was deliberately left out of that ticket's scope and filed here instead.

**Sequencing:** the Codex copy of the resolver lands with PR #477. Start after that merges, or handle only the Claude Code copy and follow up. (No graph edge: an edge would have to be added to the existing slice-5 ticket, which the rail-freeze gate forbids.)

=== THE PROBLEM ===

Two distinct failures, and closing one does not close the other:

1. **Gate bypass.** A repository that ships a package named `@adlc/context-handoff` in its own dependency tree wins resolution. It can export the four functions the hook checks for plus a numeric `HARD_BYTES`, return `{deny: false}` from `evaluateHandoffPreToolUse`, and the deny-set is simply gone. The hook's export check is a shape check, not a trust check.

2. **Secret exfiltration.** The imported module executes in the hook's process, which inherits the operator's environment — including `ADLC_MANIFEST_KEY` when one is exported. Top-level code in the planted package can read and transmit it. The manifest signing key is the trust anchor for every cross-model attestation and every gate-manifest entry: whoever reads it can forge approvals indefinitely.

PR #477 removed an explicit `manifestKey` hand-off into the resolved module (that was a regression it introduced and reverted). It did NOT and could not address the inherited environment, which is the larger half.

=== WHY THE RESOLVER EXISTS ===

Do not delete it without replacing what it does. A hook script runs from the plugin's INSTALLED location (`~/.claude/plugins/cache/...`, Codex's `PLUGIN_ROOT`), which ships no workspace `node_modules`, so a bare `import '@adlc/context-handoff'` fails there. Node 18 additionally cannot `require()` the ESM package, which is why the resolver is async. Any fix must keep the hook working from a real plugin install AND from a source checkout.

=== REQUIRED BEHAVIOUR ===

1. An enforcing hook MUST import its gate implementation only from a location the project cannot write: a plugin-owned path, a bundled/vendored copy, or a resolved realpath verified to sit inside a trusted root. A resolution that lands outside it fails closed with a distinct reason — never silently proceeds.
2. A hook process MUST NOT expose `ADLC_MANIFEST_KEY` (or any other credential) to code it imports from a location the project can influence. Prefer not launching the enforcing hook with the secret in its environment at all; scrubbing before the dynamic import is acceptable only if nothing project-controlled has executed first.
3. Both properties are proven by a test that PLANTS a hostile project-local `@adlc/context-handoff` and asserts (a) it is never imported, and (b) it cannot observe the key. A test that only checks the happy path does not close this.
4. The existing enforcing behaviour is unchanged: the frozen handoff contract suites must pass untouched.
5. Whatever replaces the walk must still work from a plugin install directory with no project `node_modules`, and on Node 18. State which mechanism was chosen and why in the hook header.
6. If the fix diverges the two resolver copies, retire `plugins/adlc-codex/hooks/test/handoff-resolve-drift.test.mjs` deliberately (replace it with whatever pins the new arrangement) rather than letting it rot.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A hostile project-local `@adlc/context-handoff` planted in a fixture repo is never imported by the Claude Code hook; the hook fails closed instead. verify: `node --test plugins/adlc-claude-code/hooks/test/handoff-resolve-trust.test.mjs`
- The same planted package cannot observe `ADLC_MANIFEST_KEY` from the Claude Code hook process. verify: `node --test plugins/adlc-claude-code/hooks/test/handoff-resolve-trust.test.mjs`
- Both properties hold for the Codex hook. verify: `node --test plugins/adlc-codex/hooks/test/handoff-resolve-trust.test.mjs`
- Each trust test proves it bites: with the guard removed the planted package IS reached, asserted against a fixture rather than by inspection. verify: `node --test plugins/adlc-claude-code/hooks/test/handoff-resolve-trust.test.mjs plugins/adlc-codex/hooks/test/handoff-resolve-trust.test.mjs`
- The hook still loads its gate and enforces from a plugin-install layout that has no project `node_modules`. verify: `node --test plugins/adlc-claude-code/hooks/test/handoff-resolve-trust.test.mjs`
- Frozen handoff contract suites pass unmodified. verify: `node --test plugins/adlc-claude-code/hooks/test/handoff-deny.test.mjs plugins/adlc-codex/hooks/test/handoff-deny.test.mjs && git diff --quiet origin/main -- plugins/adlc-claude-code/hooks/test/handoff-deny.test.mjs plugins/adlc-codex/hooks/test/handoff-deny.test.mjs`
- Package-level D1-D3 and CLI contracts still green. verify: `node --test packages/context-handoff/test/*.test.mjs packages/context-handoff/cli-test/*.test.mjs packages/context-handoff/adapter-test/*.test.mjs`
- Binding specs untouched. verify: `git diff --quiet origin/main -- docs/specs/context-rot-handoff.md .adlc/specs/context-rot-handoff.md`
- The chosen mechanism and its Node 18 / plugin-install constraints are documented where an operator will find them. verify: `rg -q 'trusted|plugin-owned' apps/docs/content/docs/integrations/claude-code.mdx apps/docs/content/docs/integrations/codex.mdx`
- The three CI gates pass on a freshly fetched base. verify: `npm run preflight`
- Trust-root tier: a distinct-provider cross-model approve is recorded before merge. verify: `node packages/prosecute/bin/adlc-prosecute.mjs tier-check --base origin/main --author-provider anthropic`

allow-suppression: none

Out of scope: the advisory/manual tier adapters (slice 6); Proven CI (slice 7); the in-process adapters (OpenCode, Pi) — they resolve through their own declared dependency, which is the plugin's supply chain rather than arbitrary project code, and are not part of this defect; changing D1-D3, band thresholds, or any deny-set semantics.
title: context-handoff: enforcing hooks must not execute project-resolved code with ambient secrets
